title: Dynamic Snake Convolution based on Topological Geometric Constraints for Tubular Structure Segmentation
mechanism: Deformable offsets constrained to a continuous chain along x or y, so the kernel follows a thin curved line. x, y and standard kernels are fused across views, with a persistent-homology loss (TCLoss).
adaptation: Put DSConv (x, y, standard, fused) in the two finest U-Net++ decoder stages only and keep the ResNet-34 encoder. Leave TCLoss out of the first arm. 76 to 88% of EL crack components are under 20 px, so expect gains mainly on long cracks and E1 long cracks.
min_experiment: DSConv decoder vs house, 5 v 5 seeds. Metrics: test-clean crack relF1@2, components >= 20 px found, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no metric improves by >= 0.012.
evidence: R (full text): DRIVE Dice 82.06, clDice 82.07. Massachusetts Roads Dice 78.21, clDice 87.64, at most +1.31 Dice and +0.77 clDice over U-Net. 3D coronary +3.40 Dice.
prior_overlap: None. BRIEF lists snake and deformable convolutions as never tried. Topology losses (clDice, Skeleton Recall) were run, but TCLoss was not.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace the two highest-resolution U-Net++ decoder blocks (optionally encoder layer1) with DSConv-x + DSConv-y + 3x3 fused, 1-ch 512 px, 24 classes. Drop TCLoss initially (topology losses already run). Judge on detection and E1, not strict IoU, because labels are jittered.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ with DSConv decoder blocks, house and PF, 5 seeds; baseline house / PF 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, components >=20 px found, E1 relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: relF1@2 and components-found gains both < 0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02.
